title: The Sparrow's House of Wax
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Chimni the sparrow
cast.description: Careful, kind mother sparrow, sweet but sharp

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Marathi tradition. Every child in Maharashtra knows this nursery tale. It is called... The Sparrow's House of Wax.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [sing-song] Every child in Maharashtra knows how this story begins. The sparrow's house was made of wax... and the crow's house was made of dung.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sparrow, Chimni, had built slowly and carefully. She collected beeswax drop by drop and shaped it into a snug little house, with a door that shut tight.

lines.speaker: kavla
lines.text: [cawing laugh] Caw caw! All that work for a house? Mine took one afternoon!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [amused] He had slapped his house together out of cow dung, and spent the rest of the summer cawing on rooftops.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the monsoon arrived. The rain came down in sheets for days. Kavla's dung house melted, slid off the branch... and was gone.

lines.speaker: kavla
lines.text: [shivering, whiny] Chimnitai, Chimnitai, open the door! My house has washed away!

lines.speaker: chimni
lines.text: [sweetly] Wait a moment. I am bathing my baby.

lines.speaker: chimni
lines.text: Wait a moment. I am feeding my baby.

lines.speaker: chimni
lines.text: Wait a moment, I am putting my baby to sleep. [short pause] There. Come in, and warm yourself by the stove.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [conspiratorial] But the crow was a crow. When the sparrow stepped out, he ate up all the food she had stored for her baby... and pretended to be asleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When she came home and found the pots empty, she understood. Without a word, she heated the iron ladle in the stove, and set it, very lightly, against the crow's tail feathers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [laughs] Kavla shot out of the house, and never came back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Marathi grandmothers end the story by reminding their grandchildren that kindness is good, but a little wax and a little sense are good too. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
